title: Redwood - NovaMed security & privacy review
summary: Redwood team walked NovaMed through their security posture and data handling guarantees. Key points: SOC 2 Type II evidence will be shared, we support SSO/SAML and RBAC with per-team roles, audit logs are retained and exportable, encryption at rest with customer KMS supported in Private deployments, hosted offering keeps short-term content for debugging unless customer opts out, and Redwood does not train models on customer data. Next steps include sending SOC2 report, security whitepaper, draft DPA, and scheduling a technical deep dive on on-prem/VPC KMS configuration.
next_steps: Sam Ortega - Send SOC 2 Type II report and security whitepaper by 2026-12-18
Priya Malhotra - Schedule technical deep dive on Private/VPC KMS and audit log export (week of 2026-12-21)
Sam Ortega - Share DPA template and data handling appendix by 2026-12-20
Customer - Confirm timeline for pilot and list of compliance reviewers by 2026-12-22
action_items: Sam Ortega - Send SOC2 Type II and ISO cert scan - 2026-12-18
Priya Malhotra - Prepare KMS integration notes and sample config - 2026-12-22
Mia Chen - Provide pilot scope and expected workloads - 2026-12-22
Sofia Alvarez - Review DPA and provide redlines - 2026-12-29
transcript:
[00:00] Sam Ortega: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I see John, Mia, Raj and Sofia are here. We'll run through Redwood's security posture and then Priya will jump into the technical parts.
[00:18] John Rivera (CISO): Thanks Sam, we really want to understand data handling, particularly around PHI/PII and whether anything could be used to train models.
[00:26] Sam Ortega: Totally. High level, Redwood offers Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. For customers with PHI we usually recommend Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys. But we'll go through details.
[00:38] Priya Malhotra (SE): Quick agenda: SOC 2/ISO status, SSO/RBAC, audit logging, encryption and KMS, data residency, and prompt retention/no-training guarantees.
[00:48] Mia Chen (CTO): Sounds good. Also want to understand how long prompts are kept and whether logs could be used to improve your models.
[00:55] Priya: Right. For Hosted, we do short-term retention for debugging and metrics, ordinarily 30 days by default, but we can contractually limit retention or disable it. And we have an explicit no-training-on-customer-data policy for all customers; we do not use customer prompts to train our global models.
[01:12] Raj Patel (Head of Data): When you say "no training" is that an internal policy, or is it enforceable in the contract? Who can attest?
[01:20] Sam: Good question. We have both contractual language in our DPA and internal controls. We'll share the DPA text; SOC 2 Type II audit also validates data segregation and access controls. We'll send the SOC 2 report after this call.
[01:35] Sofia Alvarez (Privacy Counsel): We need explicit language around PII/PHI and model training. Also audit log details: who can see content and how it's redacted.
[01:44] Priya: On audit logs: all API calls, model type, time, request/response size, and metadata are logged. Full request/response bodies are available in logs for a limited retention period, and access is RBAC-protected and audited. For Private deployments, logs can be stored in-customer VPC only.
[02:05] [02:05] Leo Zhang (Redwood): To add, audit logs include user identity from SSO if you've integrated SAML, so you get user-level traceability.
[02:12] John: What about encryption? We require AES-256 at rest and bring-your-own-key for anything that touches PHI.
[02:20] Priya: We support AES-256. For Hosted we manage keys by default, but we offer CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) integrations for Dedicated and Private. For Private, you can use your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and Redwood supports isolating keys per-tenant.
[02:40] Raj: If we use Hosted with CMEK, does that fully prevent Redwood from decrypting content?
[02:46] Priya: With proper key access controls, Redwood's control plane will not be able to decrypt contents without key access. For absolute separation we recommend Private deployment where keys never leave your environment. We'll include the KMS architecture diagram in the follow-up.
[03:02] Mia: Let's talk about data residency. Our data must remain in the EU for EU patients.
[03:09] Sam: We have regional hosting options. For Hosted customers, you can choose the EU region. Dedicated provides reserved capacity in the region. Private gives you full control over hosting. We'll map the options in the follow-up.
[03:21] John: How long are prompts retained in Hosted if we don't opt out? You said ~30 days as default; can that be shortened?
[03:28] Priya: Yes, default is configurable. We typically retain for up to 30 days for debugging and anomaly detection. We can shorten to 7 days or remove retention for an enterprise contract, and for Dedicated/Private retention can be controlled by your policies.
[03:42] Sofia: Are responses considered customer data if they contain PHI?
[03:46] Priya: Yes, anything in requests or responses is treated as customer data. Our DPA covers that.
[03:51] Raj: We run model evaluation on accuracy and hallucination. Do you ever surface customer data into your eval pipelines?
[03:58] Priya: No. We never include customer prompts or responses in our training or evaluation pipelines unless explicitly opted-in and with appropriate contractual and privacy safeguards.
[04:10] [04:10] John: Can you provide an attestation that no customer content was used to train models as of today?
[04:16] Sam: Yes, we can provide a signed attestation in the DPA and we'll include the statement in the security whitepaper we send.
[04:24] Mia: On RBAC, how granular is role control? We need per-team and per-environment separation, and ability to restrict access to raw content.
[04:33] Leo: Our RBAC supports roles (admin, developer, auditor) and custom roles. You can restrict access to request/response bodies and only allow metadata for certain roles. All access attempts are logged and part of the audit trail.
[04:49] Raj: Does RBAC integrate with our SSO?
[04:52] Priya: Yes, SAML/SSO integrates with our RBAC. We sync group membership and map to roles. We support SCIM for provisioning.
[05:00] Sofia: For audits, can logs be exported to our SIEM and retained for 7 years?
[05:06] Priya: Logs can be exported to your logging endpoint (S3, Cloud Storage, or syslog to Splunk). For Hosted customers we can forward logs to your tenant. For Dedicated/Private you control retention; Hosted can be configured to forward and then you store long-term. 7 years is feasible if you pull logs into your archive.
[05:20] John: What about redaction - can Redwood automatically redact PHI from logs?
[05:25] Priya: We offer optional PII/PHI detection and redaction in the pipeline, but that's best-effort and configurable. For strict compliance we recommend you configure ingress-level redaction or use Private deployment so data never leaves your control.
transcript_continued:
[05:40] Sam: A couple of common enterprise asks: DPA, data residency, encryption, and a signed statement on no training. We'll provide those.
[05:50] Raj: On the legal front, we need SOC 2 Type II and possibly ISO 27001. Are you certified?
[05:55] Sam: We have SOC 2 Type II and are in progress for ISO 27001; we'll send the latest evidence.
[06:03] Mia: For Private deployment, what's the on-prem operating model? Do you ship a package, or is it a managed appliance?
[06:10] Priya: Private can be deployed as a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. We provide an installable package and operator docs. You run the infrastructure; we provide support and optional managed services.
[06:23] John: If we do Private, can we ensure logs and KV cache never leave our network?
[06:29] Leo: Yes, KV cache and logs can be restricted to your VPC; we only need limited telemetry for uptime unless you opt into more support.
[06:38] Sofia: Contractually we want indemnities related to data breach and a clear incident response SLA.
[06:44] Sam: Our standard enterprise contract includes incident notification timelines and response commitments. We'll share the security SLAs and breach notification timelines in the follow-up.
[06:53] Raj: Any examples of customers using Redwood for PHI?
[06:57] Priya: We have healthcare customers in EU and US on Dedicated/Private. We'll anonymize references and provide a short case study as part of the package.
[07:07] John: How do you handle backups? Are backups encrypted and is key management tied to KMS?
[07:13] Priya: Backups are encrypted with AES-256. If you're using CMEK, backups are encrypted with your keys; otherwise we manage keys. For Private you manage backups in your environment.
[07:25] Mia: If we want to run a pilot, what telemetry do you need?
[07:29] Sam: For a pilot we usually need expected QPS, typical prompt length, P95 latency targets, and a list of integrations (SSO, KMS). That lets us size Dedicated or propose Private.
[07:41] Raj: We'll share that. Also want to know if Redwood has a process for pen testing and external audits.
[07:47] Priya: We undergo periodic pen tests and vulnerability scans; we can share summaries and a SOC assessor contact.
[07:54] Sofia: We need a clear statement on the use of third-party subprocessors.
[07:59] Sam: We maintain a subprocessors list and will provide it. For Private, subprocessors are minimal.
[08:06] [08:06] John: Can you confirm exact default retention windows and whether they can be contractual?
[08:12] Sam: Defaults: Hosted request/response bodies 30 days, aggregated metrics indefinitely at lower granularity. We will contractually set retention windows for enterprise deals. Dedicated/Private retention controlled by customer.
[08:25] Mia: For the 'no training' line, will your security whitepaper include the technical controls that enforce that (like pipeline separation, data tagging, access controls)?
[08:34] Priya: Yes, we'll include pipeline diagrams, segregation controls, and attestation language.
[08:40] Raj: If we find a PII leakage during evaluation, what's the remediation process?
[08:45] Priya: Immediate containment, log review, forensic analysis, and patching. We follow the incident response playbook and will integrate with your security contacts.
[08:55] Sofia: On legal, we want the DPA to state you won't use data for model training now or in the future without opt-in.
[09:01] Sam: Agreed. We'll include that clause; we'll flag it for legal team.
[09:07] [09:07] John: Can you show me where in the console we can disable retention or set region?
[09:12] Priya: Quick demo: Under Project Settings -> Data Controls you can toggle "Store full requests" and set retention window and region. We'll do a live demo in the technical deep dive.
[09:24] Mia: About RBAC logs: can we generate a report of who accessed content and export it to HR for audits?
[09:30] Leo: Yes, you can export user access logs per time range and include SSO identity.
[09:36] Raj: If a user is removed from SSO, is there an immediate block?
[09:39] Priya: We sync with SCIM; de-provisioning is near real-time depending on your IdP.
[09:46] Sofia: We may request background checks for any support engineers who may need access to our data during on-call. Is that possible?
[09:53] Sam: We can add support access controls and audit entries; background checks are part of our enterprise-managed support contract and can be scoped.
[10:04] Mia: Will you provide a sample SLA including MTTR for incidents involving data exposure?
[10:09] Sam: Yes, we'll share security SLA documents.
[10:12] [10:12] John: Anything else we should be aware of around model behavior and hallucinations when dealing with PHI?
[10:18] Priya: Model outputs can hallucinate. We recommend guardrails: prompt engineering, redaction, and post-processing. For sensitive data we suggest server-side filters and stricter response validation.
[10:29] Raj: Does Redwood provide policy engines or tokens to mask PHI in responses?
[10:33] Priya: We provide content filters and an optional policy enforcement hook where you can plug in your validation service before returning content to users.
[10:43] Sofia: Regarding proofs, we need signed attestations about no training on customer data, SOC2 copy, and evidence of encryption and KMS integration.
[10:51] Sam: We'll bundle that in the follow-up package.
[10:55] Mia: On compliance timelines, we need to get legal and security review done before EOY. Is that still feasible?
[11:02] Sam: We can accelerate the package; sending documents in 48 hours should keep you on track.
[11:08] [11:08] John: Ok let's recap next steps.
[11:11] Sam: Recap: We'll send SOC2 Type II report, security whitepaper with no-training attestation, DPA draft with explicit no-training clause, KMS and Private deployment architecture, subprocessors list, and schedule a technical deep dive on KMS and RBAC.
[11:25] Priya: I'll schedule the deep dive and prepare KMS config examples.
[11:29] Mia: Thanks everyone. We'll circulate pilot requirements and compliance reviewer list.
[11:34] Sam: Great. Thanks all for your time.
[11:38] [End of recording]
